title: Plan the voice, music and captions for a 60-second explainer in three languages: one consented voice, one music bed, subtitle files and a dub check
scenario: A water-filter start-up wants a 60-second explainer in English, Mexican Spanish and German. The founder's own voice reads it, with one music bed, one subtitle file per language and a dub check. Your teammate wrote the plan. You review it before the first request. Use the exhibit. The company, the people and the plan are made up for this case. The models, settings and limits are from the vendors' pages in October 2026; they change, so check the live pages before you start.
exhibit:
BRIEF (made up):
  Lumo water filter. A 60-second explainer:
  "How Lumo cleans tap water".
  Languages: English (source), Mexican Spanish, German.
  Voice: Dana, the founder. They agreed to a replica of their voice.
  Music: one calm bed under the whole 60 seconds, no singing.
  Captions: an English SRT subtitle file.
  Names: "Lumo" stays "Lumo" in every language.

PLAN (draft, made up):
  Voice     Gemini voice replication of Dana.
            Reference: 20 s of Dana reading, studio booth, studio mic.
            Consent: Dana reads Google's exact statement into their
            phone, at home, the next day.
  Script    Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS with Dana's voice. Text, line 1:
            "(warm, smiling) Meet Lumo. Clean water in ten seconds."
  Music     lyria-3-clip-preview:
            "Calm acoustic folk bed, 60 seconds, 72 BPM, soft guitar.
             Instrumental only, no vocals."
  Captions  ElevenLabs Scribe v2 on the English master, then the
            Subtitle Editor, export SRT.
            Note: "The SRT will show who is speaking and the time of
            every word, like the transcript."
  Dub       ElevenLabs Dubbing v2 in the app: en -> es-MX and de.
            If "Lumo" comes back wrong, fix the line in the app's
            dub editor. Then a native speaker watches each version.

questions.prompt: Voice: the replication may fail Google's speaker check. What should change?

options.text: Dana reads the statement in their own words so it sounds natural
options.explanation: Google asks for its exact consent statement. Own words do not meet that rule.

options.text: Record the consent in the same booth on the same studio mic
options.explanation: Right. Google says to record both clips on the same microphone in the same acoustic setting so the speaker check succeeds.

options.text: Make the reference three minutes long so the check has more audio
options.explanation: Google asks for 10 to 30 seconds of reference speech. Length is not the problem here.

options.text: Skip the consent clip, since Dana already agreed to the replica
options.explanation: Google requires two real human recordings from the same adult speaker: the reference and the consent clip.

questions.prompt: Script, line 1, on Gemini 3.8 TTS: what fits Google's guide?

options.text: Keep it, because Gemini 3.8 reads round brackets as direction
options.explanation: Google says Gemini 3.8 TTS treats the text strictly as a verbatim transcript, so the words may be spoken.

options.text: Write WARM, SMILING in capitals so the model will skip it
options.explanation: Google says capitals put stress on words. They do not hide direction from the voice.

options.text: Turn it into an angle-bracket tag, like <warm, smiling>
options.explanation: Google's angle-bracket tags are for short human sounds, like a sigh or a pause. Mood for a turn goes in style.

options.text: Take it out of the text and put "warm, smiling" in style
options.explanation: Right. Gemini 3.8 TTS reads the text as a verbatim transcript, and delivery for a turn goes in the style field.

questions.prompt: Music: what will the lyria-3-clip-preview request give you?

options.text: A 30-second clip, so use Lyria 3.5 and say 60 seconds
options.explanation: Right. Google says Lyria 3 Clip always makes 30-second clips. Lyria 3.5 length can be set in the prompt.

options.text: A 60-second track, since the prompt asks for 60 seconds
options.explanation: Google says the Clip model always generates 30-second clips, whatever the prompt says.

options.text: A song with a singer, since vocals are on by default
options.explanation: The prompt already says instrumental only, no vocals, as Google shows. Length is the problem.

options.text: An error, because Lyria makes no instrumental music
options.explanation: Google shows instrumental-only prompts, like 'Instrumental only, no vocals.' The Clip model's length is the problem.

questions.prompt: Captions: what does ElevenLabs say about the note on the SRT file?

options.text: It is right, as SRT keeps every detail of the transcript
options.explanation: ElevenLabs says subtitles have no speaker labels and no word-level timestamps.

options.text: It is wrong: subtitles have cue times and no speaker labels
options.explanation: Right. ElevenLabs says subtitles have only cue start and end times, and no speaker names or labels.

options.text: It is right only if you export VTT instead of an SRT file
options.explanation: Both are subtitle formats. ElevenLabs says subtitles have no speaker labels or word-level timestamps.

options.text: It is right only when the subtitles use Scribe v2 Realtime
options.explanation: The model is not the issue. ElevenLabs says subtitles have no speaker labels or word timestamps.

questions.prompt: Dub: "Lumo" comes back wrong in German. What does ElevenLabs say?

options.text: Fix the line in the v2 app editor and redo only that line
options.explanation: ElevenLabs says Dubbing v2 is automatic and has no in-app editor.

options.text: Set cloning strength to 10 so the dub keeps the name
options.explanation: Cloning strength sets how close the voice is to the speaker. It does not edit the words.

options.text: v2 has no in-app editor: use the API on Enterprise or v1
options.explanation: Right. Transcript edits for Dubbing v2 are via the API on Enterprise plans only. Or use a new v1 Dubbing Studio project (a v2 dub can't be converted).

options.text: Dub to es instead of es-MX, since dialects change names
options.explanation: The German dub is the problem, and a Spanish tag does not touch it. Dubbing v2 has no in-app editor.
